project_structure: Monorepo with pnpm workspaces: apps/web (Next.js 15 frontend), apps/api (NestJS backend), packages/mongo (MongoDB models), packages/db (Prisma), packages/utils (shared utilities). Web app uses ECharts for all visualization with lazy-loading module system. API uses BullMQ for job queues, Prisma for relational data, Mongoose for document storage.

relevant_files.rationale: Core frontend dependencies - ECharts 5.5.0 already installed, no graph-specific library present
Existing ECharts wrapper with lazy-loading module system - pattern to follow for graph chart
Reference implementation for interactive chart with click events, tooltips, and data fetching patterns
ProcessedItem schema with entities array (name, type, confidence) - source data for graph nodes
Akshare financial data service - source for financial instrument nodes (stocks, commodities)
Backend dependencies - no statistics/correlation library currently installed
Chart theming hook - required for consistent styling
Dashboard filter state management - pattern for graph filter state

patterns: ECharts lazy-loading pattern: installOnce() for dynamic module loading, ensureOptionModules() for auto-detecting required chart types. Chart components use: useQuery for data fetching, useMemo for option building, DashboardChart wrapper with theme/events/export support. Entity data structure: {name: string, type: string, confidence: number}. Financial data accessed via REST API endpoints with time range parameters.
dependencies: EXISTING: echarts@5.5.0 (supports graph/force series natively), @tanstack/react-query@5.51.0 (data fetching), zustand@4.5.4 (state management), antd@5.19.0 (UI components). REQUIRED ADDITIONS: None for basic force-directed graph (ECharts graph series built-in). OPTIONAL: simple-statistics or mathjs for correlation calculations if backend doesn't provide pre-computed correlations. Backend has no statistics library - correlation logic would need implementation or external service.
integration_points: 1) DashboardChart component (apps/web/components/echart.client.tsx) - extend installOnce() to support 'chart:graph' type. 2) GraphQL/REST API endpoint needed for entity-financial correlation data. 3) ProcessedItem.result.entities provides news entity nodes. 4) EconomicDataPoint/AkshareService provides financial instrument data. 5) Dashboard filter store for cross-chart filtering. 6) useChartTheme hook for consistent theming.
constraints: 1) ECharts graph series requires explicit module loading - must add to ensureOptionModules(). 2) No existing correlation/statistics library in backend - need to implement or add dependency. 3) Entity extraction quality varies (confidence 0-1) - may need filtering threshold. 4) Financial data granularity varies (realtime to monthly) - time alignment needed for correlation. 5) Large entity counts may impact force-directed layout performance - consider node limit or clustering.

clarification_needs.question: Which graph visualization library approach should be used for the force-directed layout?
clarification_needs.context: ECharts is already installed and supports graph/force series natively. Adding D3.js or vis-network would introduce new dependencies but offer more customization. The existing codebase exclusively uses ECharts for all charts.
options: Use ECharts graph series (built-in, consistent with codebase, simpler integration)
Add D3.js force-simulation (more control, steeper learning curve, new dependency)
Add vis-network (dedicated graph library, rich features, new dependency)

clarification_needs.question: How should entity-financial correlation be calculated?
clarification_needs.context: The system has news entities (ProcessedItem.entities) and financial data (Akshare) but no existing correlation logic. Correlation could be computed on-demand, pre-computed in batch jobs, or use simple co-occurrence counting.
options: Backend batch job pre-computes correlations (stored in DB, fast queries, stale data risk)
On-demand calculation via API endpoint (fresh data, slower response, compute cost)
Simple co-occurrence counting without statistical correlation (fast, less accurate)
